transcript.text: Alright, let's get this facilities coordination huddle started. We've got temporary power changes to sort out, and I need to hear from facilities, signal, and motor pool before I approve any hookup plan. Let's hear your site-specific requirements.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: During this morning's facilities inspection, I confirmed that the clinic's temporary transfer panel accepts only the keyed connector from Generator G-1. This means the clinic must be assigned to G-1. That finding isn't on the power-planning slide yet, so I want to make sure everyone here is aware before we finalize assignments.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a site-specific requirement from the signal side. In today's signal-equipment power audit, I confirmed that the communications shelter's conditioning unit requires the steadier output of Generator G-2 and must remain on that generator continuously during the plan. That audit hasn't been attached to the facilities request yet, so I want to make sure everyone is aware now before we finalize assignments.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Col. Morgan, I've got a site-specific requirement from the motor pool side. The maintenance bay's compressor startup must be supported by Generator G-1, and the compressor can only run from 1300 to 1500. I coordinated that window with the maintenance crew this morning, but it hasn't been posted to the daily power board yet, so I want to make sure everyone is aware before we finalize assignments.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Good, thank you all for bringing those site-specific requirements forward. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I make a decision. Maj. Patel, the clinic must go on G-1 due to the keyed connector — that's 25 kW, well within G-1's 60 kW capacity. Lt. Okafor, the communications shelter must stay on G-2 continuously — that's 15 kW, within G-2's 40 kW capacity. SFC Harding, the motor pool compressor must be on G-1 and can only run from 1300 to 1500 — that's 35 kW. Now, if I add the clinic's 25 kW and the motor pool's 35 kW together on G-1, that's 60 kW total, which is exactly G-1's rated capacity. That leaves no margin, but it doesn't exceed the limit. G-2 would carry only the communications shelter at 15 kW, leaving 25 kW of headroom. I'm comfortable approving this plan as long as the load test confirms G-1 handles the combined clinic and motor pool load without issue. Are there any objections before I settle this?
transcript.speaker: A1
